evidence.note: Early enumeration of forbidden Node build-pipeline files (package.json/vite/webpack) shows deliberate reading of anti-cheat check #2 before/while building.
Web search then curls the three pinned libraries to exact flat paths under /app/static (not a js/ subdir) — the pinned-path constraint and its trap were correctly extracted.
Repeated sha256sum of the vendored libs against the pinned digests — hash-pinning constraint (anti-cheat #1) internalized and re-verified.
Checks for >30M exec-bit binaries and forbidden build config files — evidence the agent inventoried the anti-cheat capability-shape checks.

Broad grounding in the real Mastodon wire contract: instance, verify_credentials, timelines, Idempotency-Key posting, lists, oauth/introspect (RFC 7662), admin reports (scoped), SSE streaming, trends, oauth password grant, structured reports, JSON vs HTML error planes.

reasoning: Observed actions demonstrate the agent extracted the major requirements and the obvious hard constraints (health, start.sh, pinned libs at exact flat paths, hash pins, OAuth, core endpoints) — the level-5 bar — and went beyond it by systematically probing anti-cheat file classes and grounding API shapes in the actual Mastodon contract (introspection, idempotency, admin scopes, SSE, error planes). However there is no visible categorized inventory of the UI-realism constraints (palette tolerances, exact labels, visibility icons, CSP directives, seed minima) and only shallow contract research (one search, no pagination-Link/cache-validator probing), so it falls short of the level-8 full-inventory anchor. This lands at 6, between 5 and 8.
